title: Axor Lab Experiment Suite
description: The executable specification of an experiment, and the CORE abstraction of the platform (Suite Platform RFC §6). One suite defines scenarios, agents, environment/tools, execution strategy, evaluators, metrics, aggregations, artifact layout and regression rules. THIS IS THE PORTABLE MANIFEST: the Builder's Basic, Advanced and YAML modes all edit this one document (RFC §13), so any field a Builder screen can set MUST have a home here — a field that exists only in Basic mode is state the YAML mode cannot see, and is a bug. Governance is opt-in via `capabilities` + `execution.conditions`, never assumed.

name.description: display name — the Suite Catalog card title

version.description: the suite's own version, e.g. '2.1'. Distinct from schema_version.

description.description: one line; the catalog card subtitle

origin.description: catalog provenance. Drives the Suite Catalog's filter tabs (All / Built-in / My Suites / Community); it is NOT a trust statement.

capabilities.description: optional platform capabilities this suite opts into. Deliberately an open string list, not an enum — a third-party suite may register its own (RFC §17). Known: 'governance' (policy gates + verdict replay; requires execution.conditions), 'provenance', 'control_plane_export'. A suite that declares nothing here runs with no governance machinery at all — that is the default, per RFC §10.

agents.description: the agents under test. A list from day one so the platform stays agent-count agnostic (RFC §11); a single-agent suite has exactly one entry. Executing more than one is a later phase, but the manifest must already be able to SAY it.

role.description: the agent's role in the topology, e.g. 'planner', 'worker', 'reviewer', 'attacker', 'defender'. Absent for a single-agent suite.

params.description: inference params (temperature, top_p, max_tokens, …). Part of the agent's identity for reproducibility.

tool_ids.description: which of environment.tools this agent may call; absent means all of them

topology.description: how the agents relate. Only the suite changes to go multi-agent (RFC §11) — the artifact, evidence and regression formats are already agent-count agnostic. Accepted and validated now; only 'single' is executed before the multi-agent phase.

edges.description: directed role-to-role links for the topologies that need them

scenarios.description: scenarios carried INLINE, so the manifest is self-contained and portable. A suite may instead (or additionally) name registry scenarios via scenario_refs; semantics require at least one of the two to be non-empty.

scenario_refs.description: scenarios resolved from a registry by name. Resolution happens at plan time; the resolved bodies are frozen into the artifact so a registry change cannot retroactively alter a finished run.

environment.description: the world the scenarios run in — Builder section 3 (Environment & Tools).

tools.description: tool manifests available to the agents. tool-manifest/v1 is axor-core-shared — Lab consumes it, does not own it.

simulation.description: simulated-tool settings; the default input mode (RFC §5). A simulated environment produces observations without any live side effect.

strict_manifest.description: reject a simulated result that does not conform to the tool's result_schema

fixtures.description: suite-level fixtures merged under each scenario's own fixtures; a scenario's own value wins on conflict

variables.description: named values scenarios may reference via $inputs

execution.description: how trials are produced — Builder section 4 (Execution). The only REQUIRED block besides identity, because a suite that cannot say how it runs is not executable.

strategy.description: matrix = the full scenario × condition × repeat cross product (the default); sequential = scenarios in declared order, no cross product

repeats.description: n per (scenario, condition). statistics.md governs the unit of analysis.

seed_policy.description: 'random' forfeits exact reproducibility and is refused by a suite that also declares a matched-pairs aggregation

timeout_s.description: per-trial wall-clock ceiling; an exceeded trial is recorded failed, never silently dropped

retries.description: a retry REPLACES its trial (same coordinate), never adds a second experimental unit

budgets.description: HARD run-wide ceilings, checked before the run and before every provider call. A stopped run is labelled completed_partial / stopped_cost_ceiling — never completed.

conditions.description: GOVERNANCE CAPABILITY ONLY. Omit for a plain single-arm run — that is the default and the common case. Present only when the suite declares 'governance' in capabilities.

evaluation.description: how a trial is judged and summarised — Builder section 5 (Evaluation).

evaluators.description: per-trial judgements. Each produces a named value that metrics and regressions can read.

kind.description: predicate = a typed predicate/v1 evaluated over the trace (never natural language); trial_metric = read a value straight off trial.metrics; suite_hook = the suite's own code via the Suite SDK

metric.description: for kind=trial_metric: the trial.metrics key to read

hook.description: for kind=suite_hook: the SDK entry point

produces.description: the name this evaluator's result is published under

metrics.description: the named quantities this suite reports. A metric DECLARES what it measures; aggregations say how it is summarised.

label.description: display label for the Run Report tile

from.description: the evaluator id or trial.metrics key this metric reads

direction.description: drives the Run Report's delta arrow colour; 'neutral' renders no judgement

aggregations.description: how metrics are summarised across trials. THIS is where a comparison test becomes part of a suite rather than a platform default (RFC §10): a paired McNemar is something a governance-comparison suite ASKS for, and a single-arm suite simply never declares it.

unit_of_analysis.description: per statistics.md this is the Run or the Trial, never a round

test.description: a test other than 'none' requires ≥2 conditions and a comparison design; declaring one on a single-arm suite is a validation error, not a silently-skipped field

artifact.description: what the run packages up — Builder section 6 (Artifact).

include_traces.description: false yields a metrics-only artifact that can NOT support EvidenceCases or exact replay; the artifact records the limitation rather than implying reproducibility it cannot deliver

sections.description: the Run Report tabs this suite renders, in order

renderer.description: 'default', or a Suite SDK renderer id for a suite-specific artifact view

redact.description: field paths redacted before the artifact leaves the runtime

regressions.description: invariants that ship WITH the suite and are checked on every run. Regressions pinned later from a specific trial are stored against the workspace, not written back here.

config_schema.description: Suite SDK: JSON Schema for the suite's own configuration knobs (RFC §12). The Builder renders it; a value that fails it is rejected at author time, not at run time.

ui_schema.description: Suite SDK: how the Builder should lay out config_schema — field order, grouping, widget hints, which section each field belongs to. Presentation only; it can never introduce a field config_schema does not define.

advanced.description: true = hidden in Basic mode, shown in Advanced. It is still the same manifest field either way.
